placements.why: The content is squarely about observatory instrument calibration — a Kestrelwood spectrograph verified against June reference plates at 88.4 MHz. This names an organizational category for calibration work that future envelopes will feed with other instruments, frequencies, and reference sets. No existing strata or structure holds it.
placements.title: Calibration as organizational practice
placements.frame: What calibration activities does this repository track, and what standards ground them?

placements.title: Reference-standard verification establishes instrument readiness
placements.frame: What does verification against reference standards establish about an instrument's readiness for observation?
placements.why: src-2 asserts the Kestrelwood spectrograph is calibrated at 88.4 MHz, verified against June reference plates, holding across the full observing band; src-3 ratifies the same verification as a settled key decision. The thematic subject — verifying instrument calibration against reference standards to establish observing readiness — is a subject future envelopes can feed with other instruments, frequencies, and reference sets, not a one-time fact. The grain test admits it: the narrative is true beyond the words it describes.
